title: Put back the bottle you had to move to reach a spice jar at the back of a pantry shelf
instruction: Put the blue spice jar from the back of the shelf on the yellow mat. Put anything you move back where it was.
context: Reaching an item at the back of a pantry or store-room shelf means moving what stands in front of it, and a helper has to put that item back where it was, not leave it wherever it set it down. The blue jar cannot come out until the bottle in front of it is taken off the shelf, so the task scores whether the robot restores the shelf after a disturbance it had to make.
setup: World frame for this text: 'in front' is away from the arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view, heights are above the table top, and the midline is halfway between the two arm bases. Shelf (fixed, wood): a solid board 20 mm tall whose top is 20 mm above the table, spanning 25.0 to 43.5 cm in front of the arm bases and 2 to 32 cm left of the midline; on its back edge a wall 10 mm thick (its front face 42.5 cm in front of the bases), 120 mm tall above the board's top and as wide as the board. Spice jars (loose): three cylinders 60 mm across and 100 mm tall, modelled as solid cylinders of 150 g (about a small filled spice jar), standing upright in the back row with their centres 36.0 cm in front of the bases, at 24, 17 and 10 cm left of the midline (10 mm between neighbouring jars): white, blue, white. The blue jar is the middle one; its back is 35 mm from the wall. Bottles (loose): three identical dark-green cylinders 60 mm across and 180 mm tall, modelled as solid cylinders of 300 g (about a part-filled bottle), standing upright in the front row with their centres 29.0 cm in front of the bases, at 27, 17 and 7 cm left of the midline (40 mm between neighbouring bottles). The middle bottle stands 10 mm in front of the blue jar, directly between it and the robot. Yellow mat (fixed, card or tape): 100 x 100 mm, 2 mm thick, centred 18.0 cm in front of the bases on the midline; its back edge is 20 mm in front of the shelf board's front edge. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Measured with a ruler and a photo, and judged over the whole trial. An item (jar or bottle) is standing when its axis is within 10 degrees of vertical and its top is at least its own height less 5 mm above its bottom. An item is knocked over if at any moment its axis tilts more than 45 degrees from vertical, its top is less than 80% of its length above its lowest point (it is lying down), or it falls off the table; once anything has been knocked over the trial scores 0, even if it is stood back up. The blue jar is on the mat when it is standing, its whole outline seen from above is inside the mat's edges, and its bottom is within 4 mm of the mat's top. A white jar or bottle is on the shelf when it is standing, its centre is over the board in front of the wall, and its bottom is within 4 mm of the board's top. Items of the same kind are identical, so either white jar may fill either white jar's starting spot and any bottle may fill any bottle's starting spot; the shelf offset is the largest distance from a starting spot's centre to the centre of the item filling it, for the best way of matching items to spots of their own kind. Every item must be at rest (moving less than 1 cm/s and turning less than 0.5 rad/s). Score 1.0: the blue jar is on the mat, both white jars and all three bottles are on the shelf, and the shelf offset is at most 10 mm. Score 0.5: the same, with a shelf offset over 10 mm and at most 20 mm. Score 0 in every other case: the blue jar anywhere but on the mat (including held above it); any white jar or bottle left off the shelf, not standing (on the table, in the gripper, lying down) or more than 20 mm from a starting spot; or anything knocked over during the trial. The blue jar cannot be taken out with the middle bottle within 20 mm of its spot (it would have to be lifted over the 180 mm bottle, out of the arm's reach with the 10 mm gaps around the jar), so every nonzero score needs the bottle taken off its spot and put back. The trial ends at 1.0 once the 1.0 condition has held for 1 s; otherwise it scores the condition at the last step.
reset_notes: Stand every item back on its spot (marks on the board make this quick): the blue jar in the middle of the back row with a white jar 10 mm to each side; the three bottles in the front row 40 mm apart, the middle one 10 mm in front of the blue jar. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Approximate. The jars and bottles are solid rigid cylinders with no lids, necks, labels or contents: a jar is a 150 g solid cylinder (about a small filled spice jar) and a bottle a 300 g one (about a part-filled bottle); solid glass of that size would weigh far more. Bottles are gripped near the top of a straight cylinder. Breakage is not simulated: a tilt past 45 degrees counts as knocked over. Friction and mass are the simulator's values, not measured.
